root_cause.text: In `drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c`’s `smi_work()`, the SMI sender error path failed to clear `intf->curr_msg` and free/reset `newmsg`, so the same `recv_msg` could be delivered twice and re-added to the IPMI `user_msgs` list, causing list corruption and a resulting use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says that after `sender()` fails, `smi_work()` calls `deliver_err_response(recv_msg)` and then `goto restart` “without cleaning up properly,” specifically because `intf->curr_msg is not cleared` and `newmsg still points to the message`, which makes `sender()` run again with the same message; the patch fixes this by setting `intf->curr_msg = NULL`, freeing `newmsg`, and setting `newmsg = NULL` on the error path.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description says that after `sender()` fails, `smi_work()` calls `deliver_err_response(recv_msg)` and then `goto restart` “without cleaning up properly,” specifically because `intf->curr_msg is not cleared` and `newmsg still points to the message`, which makes `sender()` run again with the same message; the patch fixes this by setting `intf->curr_msg = NULL`, freeing `newmsg`, and setting `newmsg = NULL` on the error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error-path cleanup in smi_work() by always clearing curr_msg under lock when needed before freeing the failed message.
intent_record.what: In the error-handling path inside smi_work(), the code no longer conditionally frees newmsg only when recv_msg is absent. Instead, it always clears intf->curr_msg, wraps that assignment with xmit_msgs_lock acquisition/release when run_to_completion is false, then frees newmsg and explicitly sets newmsg to NULL before jumping to restart.
intent_record.how: This ensures the interface's current-message pointer is reset even when an error response is delivered, preventing stale state from being left behind and avoiding concurrent access races when the worker is not running in run-to-completion mode. It also makes the cleanup unconditional for newmsg, eliminating the previous path where curr_msg could remain set after the message was freed or handled.

grouping_result.intent: Fix error-path cleanup in smi_work() by always clearing curr_msg under lock when needed before freeing the failed message.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes smi_work() error-path cleanup by clearing curr_msg and handling the failed message correctly, which prevents duplicate delivery, list corruption, and the resulting use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This error-path call can hand the received message back to the user-facing path without first ensuring the interface's current message state is cleared, which is the condition that allowed the same recv_msg to be delivered again and reinserted into the user_msgs list.

This is the actual delivery of the received message on the failure path; if curr_msg/newmsg state is not cleared before this point, the same message can be processed twice, leading to list corruption and use-after-free.

Freeing the SMI message here without first clearing/resetting the interface's current message state is part of the bug pattern described in the root cause, because the stale curr_msg can later be reused and the recv_msg can be re-added.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path call is part of the flawed sender failure handling in smi_work(); without the missing state reset, it can hand the same recv_msg back into the user path and enable duplicate delivery/list corruption.
This completes the error-response delivery of the received message. In the vulnerable flow, it occurs before curr_msg/newmsg are properly cleared, allowing the same recv_msg to be processed twice.
Freeing newmsg here without first ensuring intf->curr_msg is cleared/reset is part of the root cause; the stale state can later cause the same message to be re-added to user_msgs and lead to UAF.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the sender-error path failing to clear intf->curr_msg and free/reset newmsg, leading to possible double delivery of the same recv_msg. In this snippet, that error path is already handled: `cc = intf->handlers->sender(intf->send_info, newmsg);` and on failure `if (cc) { ... if (newmsg->user_data) deliver_err_response(intf, newmsg->user_data, cc); else ipmi_free_smi_msg(newmsg); goto restart; }`. The `goto restart;` means the work loop re-enters and can process the next message after the failed send, and the failed `newmsg` is explicitly handled instead of being left dangling. Therefore the buggy behavior is not present here, and the fix is already in place.
